docs.title: MILES · Maryland Integrated Land-use and Everyday-travel Simulator
docs.text: MILES (Maryland Integrated Land-use and Everyday-travel Simulator) is an agent-based modelling platform for Maryland: synthetic population, land use, school location, activities and traffic.

docs.title: About MILES
docs.text: MILES stands for Maryland Integrated Land-use and Everyday-travel Simulator: it follows Maryland's households from where they live and work to the miles they travel each day. It is an agent-based modelling platform that links a deep-generative synthetic population, the SILO land-use model, the MILES-Day activity model and MATSim traffic assignment for the Baltimore region and the state of Maryland.

docs.title: Where the parts come from
docs.text: Component Based on What MILES adds Synthetic population Conditional variational autoencoder (Borysov et al., 2019) PUMA embedding and size conditioning, PUMA marginal loss, income within band, logical repair, zone placement, workplace assignment Land use SILO engine Residential location, car ownership, workplace and school models estimated for the region; calibration and out-of-sample test Activities ABIT engine; TASHA scheduling MILES-Day: survey distributions conditioned on the day, estimated destination, stop, outing, return-home and mode models; household car allocation; joint-tour representative Traffic MATSim OpenStreetMap network with fixed speed and capacity rules; regional transit; income-based value of time; tolls

docs.title: Principles
docs.text:
• Estimated, not tuned. Behavioural models are maximum-likelihood estimates on microdata.
  • Tested on unseen data. Survey hold-out half, out-of-sample years, independent 2024 benchmarks.
  • Compared with standard methods under the same inputs and measures.
  • Residents on the roads. Trucks, commercial vehicles and through traffic are outside the model.

docs.title: Glossary
docs.text: ACS American Community Survey of the Census Bureau; PUMS is its Public Use Microdata Sample. ATUS American Time Use Survey. BIC Bayesian information criterion, used to choose between specifications. CVAE Conditional variational autoencoder: a neural network that learns a distribution of households conditional on   PUMA and household size and generates new households from it. Episode One activity of a person on the simulated day, with a type, start time, duration and location. GEH A statistic comparing hourly modelled and counted flows; values below 5 are a common target. Hold-out half The half of the travel-survey households not used in any estimation or calibration step. Inclusive value (logsum) The expected maximum utility of a lower-level choice, passed up to a higher-level choice. IPF, IPU Iterative proportional fitting and updating: reweighting methods of population synthesis. LODES Longitudinal Employer–Household Dynamics Origin–Destination Employment Statistics. MATSim Multi-Agent Transport Simulation, the assignment software. MSTM Maryland Statewide Transportation Model; source of the zone system and the car skims. PUMA Public Use Microdata Area, the smallest geography of the PUMS. %RMSE Root-mean-square error of modelled against counted volumes, as a percentage of the mean count. RTS The 2017/18 Regional Travel Survey of the Baltimore and Washington regions. SILO Simple Integrated Land Use Orchestrator, the land-use engine. Skim A zone-to-zone table of travel time, distance or cost. SRMSE Standardised root-mean-square error between two contingency tables. TASHA Travel Activity Scheduler for Household Agents, whose scheduling approach MILES-Day adopts. TVD Total variation distance between two distributions, in percentage points. WESML Weighted exogenous sample maximum likelihood, the estimator for choice-based samples.

docs.title: Acknowledgements
docs.text:
MILES builds on open-source software and public data:

  • SILO, the land-use microsimulation of the Technical University of Munich (msmobility/silo);
  • ABIT, the activity-based model of the Maryland set-up, whose engine runs MILES-Day;
  • TASHA, whose scheduling approach MILES-Day adopts;
  • MATSim and pt2matsim for the traffic and transit assignment;
  • Biogeme for the estimation of every choice model;
  • data of the U.S. Census Bureau, the Bureau of Labor Statistics, FHWA, NCES, MDOT and MDOT SHA, the Baltimore Metropolitan Council and the Metropolitan Washington Council of Governments, and OpenStreetMap contributors.

docs.title: Applying MILES
docs.text:
MILES answers "what if" questions by changing an input of one stage and running the chain from that stage on.

To test… Change Run from A toll or road charge a MATSim road-pricing file assignment A new road or lane change the road network assignment (and skims, for longer-run effects) Transit service the GTFS feeds → transit schedule and skims activities Housing or job growth in a zone land-use inputs: development capacity, job controls land use Income-based discounts toll.discount.factor, toll.discount.threshold assignment

docs.title: Case study: pricing the Baltimore Beltway (I-695)
docs.text:
Model version

This study was run with an earlier version of the chain (before the re-estimated models documented on this site). It shows what the platform can do; the numbers will be updated with the current models.

docs.title: Question
docs.text: Who would pay a toll on I-695, who would change route or stop using the Beltway, and how would the benefits and costs be distributed across income groups?

docs.title: Designs tested
docs.text:
• Uniform tolls on the Beltway.
  • An area-based scheme.
  • An income-based discount (50 % for households under $50,000), applied person by person.
  • A fixed charge per entry, to test the mechanism.

Each design was run in MATSim with the same plans and seeds as the base, and the results were broken down by person: stayers, leavers and newcomers on the Beltway, travel time and toll paid, and consumer surplus by income decile.

docs.title: What the platform showed
docs.text:
• Beltway use is spread evenly across incomes, so a uniform toll takes a larger share of income from lower-income households: the toll is regressive.
  • Every design reduced net welfare in the tests: the users' loss in consumer surplus exceeded the toll revenue.
  • The income-based discount was the only lever that reduced the regressivity, at a cost in revenue.
  • Select-link analysis traced diverted Beltway trips to other routes, such as I-83 and arterials like MD-140.

docs.title: Outputs produced
docs.text:
• welfare and revenue tables by design and income decile;
  • maps of toll incidence by home location;
  • hourly link-volume animations;
  • diversion paths of leavers.

docs.title: 1. Pick the stage
docs.text:
Short-run responses (route and departure time) need only the assignment. Responses in destination and mode need MILES-Day with new skims; long-run responses in where people live and work need the land-use model too.

Response Stages to rerun Route, departure time MATSim Destination, mode, trip making MILES-Day → MATSim Residential and workplace location, car ownership SILO → schools → MILES-Day → MATSim

docs.title: 2. A pricing scenario in MATSim
docs.text:
1. Write a road-pricing file (MATSim roadpricing format): the links, the time windows and the amount. The base file assignment/network/roadpricing_HARB_2024.xml is an example.

  2. Run the base and the scenario with the same plans and seeds:

    python pipeline/run_chain.py --sample 0.1 --iterations 100 matsim 2024 2024 1 \
       --plans population_2024_scc.xml.gz --toll my_scheme.xml

  3. Compare executed trips (output_trips.csv.gz), link volumes (link_hours_s<N>.csv.gz) and scores (output_plans.xml.gz) between base and scenario, seed by seed.

Seeds

Run at least five seeds for base and scenario. Differences smaller than the spread across seeds are noise.

docs.title: 3. Reading results by person
docs.text: Every MATSim agent carries its household income, cars, home zone and county, so changes in travel time, toll paid and utility can be summarised by income decile or by area.

docs.title: 4. Land-use scenarios
docs.text: Edit the land-use inputs (development_*.csv for building capacity, job control totals for employment), write a properties file with landuse/run/write_properties.py, and run SILO from 2016; then rerun schools, MILES-Day and MATSim on the scenario's 2024 population.

docs.title: Headline results
docs.text: Stage Test Result Synthetic population ACS 2014–18, Maryland every attribute class within 3.9 pp Land use out of sample, 2021–24 commute flows correlate 0.995 with the ACS; household size and cars within 2.1 pp in 2024 Activities survey hold-out half +1.2 % activities, start times within 2 pp per hour Assignment 2,308 count stations, 2024 0.77 of all counted vehicles carried by residents alone; R² = 0.89

docs.title: Comparison with standard methods
docs.text: Each stage is run against an established alternative. Every variant uses the same inputs, targets, hold-out data and measures; baselines are calibrated with the same levers; no variant is fitted to traffic counts.

docs.title: Population synthesis: CVAE against IPF, IPU and weighted sampling
docs.text:
Baselines: iterative proportional fitting with a weighted draw, iterative proportional updating (PopulationSim) and weighted sampling of the training households, all on the same training records and controls, five draws each.

  • On fit to the held-out records, the classic methods are better: IPU reaches the noise level of the held-out data on one-way distributions.
  • Reweighting methods copy whole training households, so they cannot produce a combination that is absent from the sample. The CVAE generates 62 % of the held-out combinations that the training data lack, and copies fewer households than a fresh sample shares with the training data (11 % against 22 %).

The CVAE's gain is variety beyond the sample, not closer fit to it.

docs.title: Land use: against the original SILO Maryland model
docs.text:
Both models are calibrated with the same procedure and tested on 2021–2024.

Measure Original MILES Out-of-sample cells within 5 pp 86.8 % 94.5 % Mover flows between counties, correlation with ACS 0.625 0.946 Movers staying in their county, share of observed 0.260 0.986 Mean travel time to work, ratio to ACS 1.557 0.974

The gap of the original model lies in young adults living with their parents, age, cars, employment, household size and income.

docs.title: Activities: against the original set-up and a standard tour-based model
docs.text:
• MILES-Day beats both baselines on 58–73 % of the error measures and loses on 2–21 %, in all three survey settings; its mean normalised error is less than half of theirs.
  • The gain comes mainly from the TASHA-type scheduler (durations, start times, school and work activity) and from the return-home and workplace-outing models: adding TASHA-type generation cuts the mean normalised error from 9.9 to 6.8 on the estimation half, and the return-home and outing models bring it to 4.0.
  • On the 2024 external data no variant is clearly best.

docs.title: Calibration
docs.text: Calibration is confined to three groups of land-use and workplace parameters. The calibration window is 2017–2020; the years 2021–2024 are kept for the out-of-sample test. Traffic counts play no role.

docs.title: Demographic levers
docs.text:
Five levers scale the event rates of SILO: births, marriages, divorces, the shift \(a_m\) of the moving decision and leaving the parental home. Targets come from the Census components of change and the ACS PUMS. In each round the model is run from 2016 to 2020 and every lever is updated by the damped ratio

\[ \theta^{(k+1)} = \theta^{(k)} \big(y^{\text{obs}} / y^{\text{model}}\big)^{\omega}, \]

where \(y\) are the window means of 2017–2020 and \(\omega\) is a damping exponent between 0.5 and 1.0.

Lever Model / target, final round Births 1.002 Marriages 1.000 Divorces 1.000 Moves 1.000 Leaving home 0.988

The levers are then frozen, and the model is run from 2016 to 2024 with five seeds.

docs.title: Car ownership
docs.text: The county constants of the car-ownership model are updated by the damped log-ratio of observed to modelled shares. In the final round every county × car-ownership cell is within 5 percentage points of the ACS.

docs.title: District of Columbia workplace term
docs.text: The travel survey has more Maryland workers commuting to the District than the ACS: the estimated model gives 13.1 % against 9.8 %. For application, the District workplace term is shifted by −0.387 (from 1.097 to 0.710), so that 9.82 % of Maryland-resident base-year workers work in the District, the ACS 2016–2020 share. This share is therefore not a test of the model.

docs.title: Not calibrated
docs.text:
• MILES-Day is applied without frequency factors or constant adjustments.
  • None of the other choice models is calibrated.
  • The choice-based weights of the work tour mode choice are part of its estimator.
  • The road network is not calibrated to counts.

docs.title: Common design
docs.text:
• Sample. All survey-based models are estimated on the estimation half of the travel survey; the land-use models of residential location and car ownership on ACS PUMS households.
  • Weights. The survey is stratified by home location, which every model except residential location takes as given, so these models are estimated without weights. Weights are used only where the sample is selected on the outcome: the zone level of residential location (whose outcome is the home location) and the work tour mode choice (whose sample over-represents rail commuters; weighted exogenous sample maximum likelihood).
  • Location probabilities. A survey location known by traffic zone or tract may cover several model zones; its probability is the sum of the probabilities of those zones, weighted by housing units, enrolment or jobs.
  • Choice sets. School and activity-location models use the full choice set of 1,588 zones; workplace choice the chosen zone and 99 sampled zones; the zone and dwelling levels of residential location 30 sampled alternatives.
  • Specification search. Each model is built in blocks of variables from a basic model. A block is kept when its likelihood-ratio test is significant at 5 %, it lowers the BIC and its signs are as expected; non-nested forms are compared by BIC.
  • Standard errors are robust (sandwich).
  • Software: Python Biogeme for every model of the estimation package.

docs.title: Linking logsums
docs.text:
Three logsums connect the models:

  • Mode-choice logsum of a person between two zones for a purpose, from the tour mode model; it enters the stop models as the logsum detour.
  • Non-work accessibility of a zone, the destination-choice logsum over all 1,588 zones for shopping, recreation, accompanying and other trips, weighted by trip shares (0.329, 0.279, 0.148, 0.243). It enters residential location, car ownership and workplace choice.
  • Inclusive values of the residential location levels.

docs.title: Re-estimating the models yourself
docs.text: Every model can be re-estimated from its data with Python Biogeme; see the estimation package.

docs.title: Known limitations
docs.text: No feedback from the assignment. The land-use and activity models read fixed skims. Assigned morning-peak car times are a median 0.78 of the skim   times on which locations were chosen. Weak response to time and cost in mode choice. All time and cost coefficients are negative and significant but small. A 20 % higher car operating cost lowers   car-driver kilometres by about 0.2 % (elasticity about −0.01), below the published range; the transit-time   elasticity is about −0.2. The models reproduce current mode shares through their constants and socio-economic   terms and respond weakly to price and time. Activity frequencies do not respond to travel conditions. Frequencies, start times and durations come from survey distributions. They depend on the day's work or school   episode, not on travel time, cost or the calendar year. Activity levels of 2024. The model keeps the workplace attendance of 2017/18. More residents have a work activity than in the 2021–2024 time   use survey, and discretionary activities do not follow the fall after 2019. Moves after 2020. The calibrated move rate stays at its 2017–2020 level, while the observed rate fell after 2020. Residents only on the roads. Trucks, commercial vehicles, visitors and through traffic are not modelled. Volumes fall short of counts outside   the peaks and on roads with much freight. Correlated distance terms in the stop models. The stop models combine highly correlated distance terms (variance inflation factors up to 32), each kept because   it lowers the BIC; their individual coefficients are less precise than the fit suggests. Repeated use of the hold-out half. The hold-out half was consulted more than once in the specification search of several models, so its fit is not a   fully independent test.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
Every stage is tested on data it was neither estimated nor calibrated on. Verification compares a model with its estimation data; validation with data used in no estimation or calibration step. Each stage page shows the same things: headline numbers, the main figure, every comparison in detail, and a scorecard.

Stage Tested against Comparisons Within Close Outside Synthetic population ACS PUMS 2014–18, held-out PUMS test split, LODES, travel survey 31 25 3 3 Land use ACS, Census estimates, JOLTS, permits, county flows; out of sample 2021–24 36 27 6 3 School location Survey students, ACS enrolment 8 2 4 2 Activities Survey hold-out half; ATUS, ACS 2024, LODES 43 25 13 5 County view Every variable by county, all 24 Maryland counties 336 282 51 3

Traffic is compared as a ratio rather than counted against a limit, because the model carries residents only: simulated passenger-vehicle volumes are 0.81 of the 2024 counts at 2,308 mainline stations (R² 0.90 across stations); see Traffic.

Within: a distribution within 5 percentage points (total variation distance), a set of shares within 5 points on average (mean absolute difference) or a rate within 5 % (mean absolute percentage error) of the observed value, the acceptance limits of the land-use and activity tests. Close: within twice that. Outside: beyond.

docs.title: Strategy
docs.text:
Each stage is estimated on one set of data and tested on another:

Stage Estimated on Tested on Synthetic population ACS PUMS 2012–16, 80 % training split by PUMA 10 % held-out test split; ACS 2014–18 by PUMA Land use ACS PUMS movers 2014–18; survey estimation half; calibrated on 2017–20 Movers 2019–21 (out of time); ACS and Census 2021–24 (out of sample) Schools Survey estimation half Survey hold-out half; ACS enrolment Activities Survey estimation half (10,889 households) Survey hold-out half (10,899 households); chain test on the synthetic population; ATUS, ACS and LODES for 2024 Traffic Nothing estimated; network from fixed rules 2024 counts, continuous counters, screenlines, mileage

The 2017/18 Regional Travel Survey is split at random into two halves by household, stratified by home county and household size. The hold-out half enters no estimation or calibration step. TASHA was validated on a later survey of the same region; no later diary exists here, so the hold-out half and the 2024 benchmarks take its place (details).

docs.title: Estimation and validation strategy
docs.text:
TASHA was estimated on the 1996 Transportation Tomorrow Survey of Toronto and validated on the 2001 survey, a different year (Roorda, Miller and Habib, 2008). No regional travel diary has been collected in Baltimore and Washington since the 2017/18 Regional Travel Survey, so MILES-Day replaces the second survey year with a split of the households and with independent sources for the forecast year.

TASHA (Roorda et al., 2008) MILES-Day Estimation data Toronto travel survey, 1996 Regional Travel Survey 2017/18, estimation half (10,889 households) Verification Same survey, same households Estimation half: the model run on the observed households it was estimated on Validation Toronto travel survey, 2001 (another year) Hold-out half (10,899 households), drawn at random by home county and household size, used in no estimation or calibration step Chain test – The model run on the synthetic population, compared with the hold-out half: separates the error of the activity model from that of the population Forecast year 2001 households 2024 population of the land-use model against independent sources: ATUS 2021–24 time use, ACS 2024 commute, LODES flows Replications – Ten per test; bands show their 90 % range Measures Start time, duration by start hour, trips per chain, distance by start hour; Kolmogorov–Smirnov D and P on hourly values The same four, the same statistic; plus activities, distances and tour modes by type

Every distribution, frequency and coefficient of MILES-Day comes from the estimation half; none is adjusted to the hold-out half or to 2024 data. The hold-out half was consulted more than once during the specification search of some models, so its fit is close to, but not fully, an independent test.

How to read the figures

Orange: model; dark grey: observed; light grey: a second observed source. Error bars: range of the five land-use seeds or of the ten activity-model replications. Each panel shows one fit measure: for a distribution the total variation distance (TVD, percentage points of the population that would have to change class); for shares that are not one distribution, the mean absolute difference (MAD, percentage points); otherwise the mean absolute percentage error (MAPE).

docs.title: Why some comparisons are outside
docs.text:
Home-county workplace share by county (18.6 points). The model keeps 41–90 % of each county's employed residents working in their home county, against 24–72 % in LODES; the difference averages 18.6 points and is the same in the base year (17.2 points in 2016), so it does not grow during the simulation. The two measure different things: LODES counts jobs from employer records, and multi-establishment employers can report jobs at one address; the model's workplace choice is estimated on the travel survey, which records where workers go. Against the ACS, which also asks workers, the commute agrees: county-to-county flows correlate at 0.995, and the 2024 activity model sends 54.4 % of commuters to their home county or county group against 54.0 % in the ACS.

Dwelling vacancy by county (2.1 points on average). This is a weakness of the land-use model. County populations are held to the Census estimates and new dwellings follow the county building permits, so vacancy is what is left between the two. Where the residential-location model sends more households than there are dwellings, vacancy runs to zero and the county falls short of its population: Carroll (0 % vacant, 5.6 % short of the Census) and Prince George's (0 %, 2.5 % short). Where it sends fewer, vacant dwellings accumulate: Howard 10.4 % and Baltimore City 7.7 % against 2.3 % and 4.9 % in the ACS. Construction does not respond to vacancy, and prices respond too weakly to rebalance demand across counties.

Vacant share of jobs (imposed; 1.2 points on average, 4.3 points in 2021). Jobs follow the job inputs (LODES, QCEW) year by year, while employment is aligned to the ACS rate of the year before the simulated year. The vacancy is the difference, so it inherits that lag: in 2021 the model leaves 2.7 % of jobs vacant against 7.0 % in JOLTS, when openings surged after the pandemic, a surge that is in no input. By 2024 the two are close again (5.5 against 5.1 %).

docs.title: Why the car time to school is too long
docs.text: The assigned schools are 1 to 4 minutes farther than the schools of the survey students (2024: K–8 14.9 against 13.7 min, high school 17.5 against 15.7, college 34.7 against 30.3). Most of the gap is present in the base year (2016: 14.9, 16.8 and 33.0 min), and it grows slowly for high school and college as the population moves while the school inventory and its capacities stay fixed. Enrolment is an upper limit, enforced by shadow prices, so students who do not find a seat at a near school are sent to a farther one. The observed times are those of the 2017/18 survey students, so the 2024 comparison also carries seven years of change in where students live.

docs.title: Developers
docs.text:
MILES combines Python stages with three Java engines. This section documents the code: which classes and scripts MILES adds or changes, how they are wired, and how to extend them.

  • Population code

    The CVAE library and the post-processing steps.

  • SILO engine changes

    Residential location, car ownership and workplace choice in the engine.

  • MILES-Day engine

    The abm.models.maryland package: generation, destinations, mode choice.

  • MATSim runner

    RunBaltimoreToll: scoring, value of time, tolls.

  • Pipeline

    Orchestration, plans converter, skims and accessibility.

  • Estimation package

    One folder and notebook per model, with Biogeme.

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text:
• Coordinate system: EPSG:26985.
  • Skims: gzipped CSV FROM,TO,VALUE.
  • Coefficients live in CSV files read by the engines; every file is written by a script from the estimation results, never by hand.
  • Unit checks compare engine utilities with Biogeme's \(X\beta\) (landuse/checks/check_*.py, activity/checks/check_engine_utilities.py).
  • Paths: each script keeps the project root in a constant at its top (ROOT or V).

docs.title: MILES-Day engine
docs.text: MILES-Day runs on the ABIT engine (msmobility/abit). Its own code is the package abm.models.maryland and the run class abm.RunAbitMarylandLos, in activity/engine/ABIT/src/main/java.

docs.title: Classes
docs.text: Class Role abm.RunAbitMarylandLos entry point; args[0] = properties file; seed from -Dabit.seed abm.models.ModelSetupMaryland wires the sub-models; mode.choice.model = tour_nl selects the tour mode model abm.io.input.MarylandLosDataReader reads zones, skims, the land-use households, persons, jobs, dwellings, schools and workplaces MarylandTashaGenerator generation and scheduling from the survey distributions; outings, return home, stop relocation, tours (tasha.generation=true) MarylandDestinationChoice destination and stop logits over all zones (dest.choice.model=mnl) MarylandTourNestedModeChoice tour mode choice by segment; household stage (joint tours, car allocation) WorkAttendance daily work attendance MarylandFullModeChoice, MarylandTourModeChoice, MarylandFrequencyGenerator, MarylandStopModel, … earlier paths, kept but switched off

docs.title: What happens per household
docs.text:
Households run in parallel, each with its own random stream.

flowchart TD
  A[Joint episodes<br/>frequency, start, duration, participants, place] --> B[Each member's agenda<br/>types in precedence order]
  B --> C[Outings from the workplace]
  C --> D[Clean-up of short work and lunch-at-home episodes]
  D --> E[Chains: return-home logit]
  E --> F[Main destinations and stops: location logits]
  F --> G[Tours and tour modes]
  G --> H[Household stage: joint tours together, cars allocated]
  H --> I[Outing modes; transit leg modes]
  I --> J[activities.csv, legs.csv]

Agenda order: WB, WAHB, PW, SW, RHW, SCH, JO_REC, JO_OTH, JS, IO_REC, IO_ACC, IO_OTH, IS. A conflict is resolved by shifting the episode (up to 30 min), then shortening it (to half), then redrawing it (up to 10 times).

docs.title: Coefficient set: activity/parameters/
docs.text:
File Holds run_params.csv model switches appended to the properties tour_mode_choice.csv tour mode coefficients: work, school, shopping, other, joint shopping, joint other parking_paid_share.csv paid-parking share by destination area dest_choice_mnl.csv destination and stop logits (primary, stops, school/daycare, work business, home workers, outings) tasha/tasha_frequency.csv, tasha_start.csv, tasha_duration.csv survey distributions tasha/tasha_joint_*.csv joint episodes: participants and propensity tasha/tasha_return_home.csv return-home logit tasha/tasha_subtour.csv outing generation and mode tasha/tasha_transit_legs.csv transit leg modes tasha/tasha_params.csv scheduler parameters, worker-type shares, file names TERM_MAP.csv every estimated term → engine file and variable

activity/build_parameters.py writes this set from the estimation outputs and records a checksum of every source in build_state.json.

docs.title: Run
docs.text:
python activity/run_activity_model.py myrun --coef activity/parameters --seed 1 --sample 0.1 --threads 6 --xmx 13g --year 2024

This copies the coefficient set into the run folder and starts java -Dabit.seed=N -Djava.library.path=… abm.RunAbitMarylandLos <properties>.

docs.title: Estimation package
docs.text: The estimation package lets anyone re-estimate every model of MILES with Python Biogeme and check the result against the published estimates. It lives in estimation/package/; the specification search behind each model is in estimation/development/.

docs.title: Layout
docs.text:
estimation/package/
├── RUN_ORDER.pdf                 which folder to run, in which order
├── SILO/                         land-use, workplace and school models (8)
│   ├── 00_shared_data/           (not in the repository) census microdata, survey, zones, skims
│   ├── 01_residential_county/
│   │   ├── INSTRUCTIONS.pdf      from data download to output, step by step
│   │   ├── 01_residential_county_estimation.ipynb
│   │   ├── input/code/           data preparation scripts
│   │   ├── input/data/raw/       source extracts
│   │   ├── input/data/estimation/  the estimation table and its data dictionary
│   │   ├── input/data/holdout/   hold-out sample
│   │   ├── model/                Biogeme script, published estimates
│   │   └── output/               your results
│   └── ...
├── ABIT/                         MILES-Day: distributions and 20 models
│   ├── 00_tasha_distributions/   activity distributions (not a Biogeme model)
│   ├── 01_primary_destination_pooled/
│   └── ...
└── tools/                        notebook and instruction builders

docs.title: The models
docs.text: Folder Model SILO/01 Residential location: county SILO/02 Residential location: zone × structure type SILO/03 Residential location: dwelling SILO/04 Car ownership SILO/05 Workplace choice SILO/06–08 School location: K–8, high school, college ABIT/00 Activity distributions (frequency, start, duration, joint) ABIT/01 Main destination, four purposes pooled ABIT/02–05 Stops: shopping, recreation, accompanying, other errands ABIT/06 Outing from the workplace: first stop ABIT/07–08 Work business: usual-workplace workers; other persons ABIT/09 Work trips of home workers ABIT/10 School without record and daycare, pooled ABIT/11–13 Outing generation, outing mode, return home ABIT/14–19 Tour mode: work, school, shopping, other, joint shopping, joint other ABIT/20 Transit leg mode

docs.title: The notebooks
docs.text:
Every model folder has a notebook, <folder>_estimation.ipynb, that runs from the raw data to the estimates:

  1. Raw data and where to download it
  2. Data preparation steps
  3. The estimation table and its data dictionary
  4. Descriptive statistics and choice shares
  5. Correlation heatmaps and variance inflation factors of the variables in the utilities
  6. The model specification (the folder's Biogeme script, unchanged)
  7. Log-likelihood at the published coefficients
  8. Biogeme estimation
  9. Estimates in the published format, fit, comparison with the published values, correlation of the estimates
  10. Hold-out log-likelihood

Open a notebook in VS Code, select the kernel Python (biogeme) and run all cells. Switches at the top choose what is recomputed; the largest models (schools, stops, the location models) default to reading saved results, because their estimation needs more memory than a laptop has.

docs.title: From the command line
docs.text:
cd estimation/package/SILO
./run_model.sh 04_car_ownership     # check, estimate, compare; log in 04_car_ownership/output/run_log.txt
./run_all.sh                        # all SILO models in order

docs.title: Data
docs.text: The repository holds the scripts, notebooks and published estimates of every model, but not the estimation tables: they are built from the census microdata and the travel survey by each folder's input/code scripts. Each folder's INSTRUCTIONS.pdf lists the downloads, from raw data to estimates.

docs.title: How estimates reach the engines
docs.text:
Estimation output Engine file Residential location, car ownership, workplace, schools landuse/engine_inputs/, landuse/schools/parameters/ (via landuse/coefficients/write_residential_location.py–e04) Tour mode choice activity/parameters/tour_mode_choice.csv Destinations and stops activity/parameters/dest_choice_mnl.csv Return home, outings activity/parameters/tasha/tasha_return_home.csv, tasha_subtour.csv Activity distributions activity/parameters/tasha/tasha_frequency.csv, tasha_start.csv, tasha_duration.csv

activity/build_parameters.py writes the activity files and TERM_MAP.csv, which maps all 699 estimated terms to their engine file and variable.

docs.title: MATSim runner
docs.text:
assignment/engine/matsim-run is a Maven project on MATSim 2024.0 with the road-pricing contrib.

Class Role de.umd.matsim.RunBaltimoreToll main runner: configuration, scoring, value of time, tolls DistanceConstrainedPermissibleModes removes walk and bike beyond a maximum distance when mode choice is on RunBaltimore earlier runner without tolls 
java -Xmx32g -Dseed=1 -Dthreads=12 -Dincome.vot.form=usdot -cp baltimore-matsim-1.0.jar \
  de.umd.matsim.RunBaltimoreToll network.xml.gz plans.xml.gz transitSchedule.xml.gz transitVehicles.xml.gz out/ 100 0.1 0.178 roadpricing.xml

docs.title: Built-in settings
docs.text: Setting Value Simulation QSim 0–36 h, car as main mode, stuck time 120 s Replanning re-route 0.15, departure-time mutation 0.10 (±30 min), plan selection the rest; plan memory 5 Modes fixed from MILES-Day; ride routed on the car network; walk and bike teleported (beeline × 1.3) Transit SwissRailRaptor; search radius 4,000 m Scoring performing 0.78 utils/h; per-person marginal utility of money = 0.78 / value of time Value of time usdot: 0.5 × household income / 2,080 h, income at least $5,000 Monetary distance rate car and ride $0.075/km Activities duration bins per type; shops open 8:00–20:00 Coordinate system EPSG:26985

docs.title: Tolls
docs.text: Toll schemes are MATSim road-pricing files passed as the last argument, for example assignment/network/roadpricing_HARB_2024.xml ($3.00 per crossing of the two harbour tunnels). toll.discount.factor and toll.discount.threshold give income-based discounts.

docs.title: Pipeline
docs.text: File Role run_chain.py orchestrator: land-use step, activities, MATSim plans, MATSim, skims, loop activities_to_matsim.py MILES-Day output + land-use persons → MATSim plans snap_to_network.py moves activities off car links outside the connected network skims_from_matsim.py AM-peak car skims from MATSim events transit_skim.py, TransitSkim.java transit skims with SwissRailRaptor accessibility.py zone accessibility by year for the land-use models

docs.title: Bookkeeping
docs.text: Every stage writes <stage>/.done.json with its inputs, outputs, checksums, duration and settings, and is skipped next time unless --force is given. Completed stages are appended to registry.jsonl; logs go to pipeline/logs/. --dry-run prints the full command sequence.

docs.title: Plans converter
docs.text:
python pipeline/activities_to_matsim.py --activities A --legs L --pp pp_2024.csv --hh hh_2024.csv \
       --out population.xml.gz [--expansion 10] [--residents-only] [--no-gateways] [--seed 20260707]

One weekday per person; tours cut to the Baltimore region (internal, inbound, outbound); homes on residential buildings and other activities on points of interest of the matching type in the zone.

docs.title: Feedback loop
docs.text: run_chain.py loop runs land use, activities and MATSim in two-year steps from 2016 to 2026 and feeds MATSim travel times back as skims, repeating a validation year until county population changes by less than 0.5 % and zone accessibility by less than 2 % (at most three repeats).

docs.title: Population code
docs.text: population/cvae is a small PyTorch package with numbered steps; population/post adapts its output to the land-use model.

docs.title: Library: population/cvae/vaelib
docs.text: Module Role config paths, recode maps, income bands, cardinalities (base year 2016; up to 7 persons; 18 age bands) pums_io, preprocessing, crosswalks read and recode the PUMS; zone ↔ PUMA ↔ county dataset tensors and the 80/10/10 split by PUMA model the conditional VAE: one-hot input, PUMA embedding, encoder, decoder, household and person heads train cross-entropy + KL with free bits, β annealing, PUMA marginal loss, EMA, early stopping targets, generate PUMA targets; sampling income_bins dollar income drawn within the band from the PUMA's records consistency logical rules applied after sampling zones, dwelling, workplace, silo_export zone placement, dwelling attributes, workplaces, SILO files validate, diagnostics, analysis held-out validation and figures

docs.title: Steps: population/cvae/steps
docs.text:
Step Does Writes 00_analyze_raw_acs.py statistics of the raw PUMS outputs/00_raw_analysis/ 01_preprocess.py recode to the SILO schema 01_preprocessed/{hh,pp}.parquet 02_build_targets.py PUMA marginal targets 02_targets/ 03_train.py train 03_training/<tag>/checkpoint_best.pt, history, split 04_generate.py sample households 04_generated/{hh,pp}.parquet 05_workplace.py workplaces 05_workplace/ 06_silo_export.py dwellings, SILO CSV 06_silo_input/{hh,pp,dd,jj}_2016.csv 07_validate.py test-split validation 07_validation/<tag>/ 08_figures.py, 09_study_areas.py figures; county checks

Training options: --epochs --latent --hidden --enc-depth --dec-depth --free-bits --beta --w-marginal --tag --smoke.

docs.text: Script Does rebalance_population.py redraw households per PUMA to ACS household and age controls; place them in zones zone_weights_2016.py, zone_weights_2020.py occupied housing units per zone from Census blocks employment_2016_lodes.py jobs by zone and type from LODES market_vacancy_2016.py, zone_vacancy_2016.py vacant dwellings on the market workplace_balanced.py gravity workplaces for residents outside the workplace-model area export_silo_base.py final 2016 base files validate_stage1*.py, figures_stage1.py validation tables and figures

docs.title: SILO engine changes
docs.text: MILES runs on SILO (msmobility/silo), commit 3066ca9. Its changes are shipped as landuse/engine/silo_changes.patch (modified files) and landuse/engine/src/ (new files at their package paths).

docs.title: Classes
docs.text:
Class Module Status Role ReslocModel useCases/maryland changed three-level nested logit: county → zone × dwelling type → dwelling ReslocProperties useCases/maryland changed reads the resloc.* keys ReslocRespecUtility useCases/maryland new utilities of the estimated residential location model, shared by engine and verifier ReslocRespecVerify useCases/maryland new compares engine utilities with the estimation CarOwnershipModelMd useCases/maryland changed 0/1/2/3+ car logit with coefficients from file CarOwnershipRespec useCases/maryland new utility of the estimated car-ownership model JobDataManagerImpl siloCore changed vacant-job workplace choice with the estimated model JobDataProperties siloCore changed job.choice.*, job.search.impedance.file

Main class: de.tum.bgu.msm.run.SiloMstm.

docs.title: Build and run
docs.text:
mvn compile -pl siloCore,extensions/schools,useCases/maryland
bash landuse/run/run_silo.sh landuse/run/<scenario>.properties 28g

run_silo.sh uses JDK 21, puts the compiled modules and landuse/run/classpath.txt on the class path and logs to run/logs/<scenario>.log.

docs.title: From estimates to engine files
docs.text:
Script Writes coefficients/write_residential_location.py residential_county_coefficients.csv, residential_zone_dwelling_coefficients.csv, county and zone attributes coefficients/write_car_ownership.py car_ownership_estimated_coefficients.csv, car_ownership_puma_attributes.csv coefficients/write_workplace_choice.py workplace_choice_coefficients.csv coefficients/write_school_location.py school coefficients (landuse/schools/parameters/) coefficients/write_zone_attributes.py zone attributes

Checks: landuse/checks/check_*.py recompute utilities in the engine and compare them with \(X\beta\) from the estimation; the verifiers are switched on with -Dsilo.resloc.respec.dump and -Dsilo.jobchoice.verify.

docs.title: Adding a model
docs.text:
1. Estimate it and write its coefficients to a CSV in landuse/engine_inputs/.
  2. Read the file in a properties class and add a switch key.
  3. Implement the utility in a pure class (as ReslocRespecUtility), so the engine and a verifier share it.
  4. Add a unit check that compares engine utilities with the estimation.

docs.title: Get started
docs.text:
MILES runs as five stages. Each stage can be run on its own from the outputs of the previous one, or the whole chain can be driven by the pipeline.

  • Installation

    Python environments, Java 21, Maven and the three engines.

  • Repository layout

    Where each component lives.

  • Run the chain

    The commands, stage by stage.

  • Runtime and storage

    How long each stage takes and how much memory and disk it needs.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text: Software Version Used by Python 3.10 or later every step Java (JDK) 21 SILO, MILES-Day, MATSim Maven 3.9 or later building the Java engines Memory 32 GB or more SILO (24–28 GB heap), MILES-Day (13 GB), MATSim (32 GB)

docs.title: 1. Get the code and the miles command
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/Tomal121186621/MILES.git
cd MILES
python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -e ".[population,docs]"
miles --help

pip install -e . installs the miles command from your clone, so it always runs the code you have checked out.

docs.title: 2. Configure
docs.text:
cp miles.example.toml miles.toml

Set paths.workspace to the folder that holds the data and receives the runs, and the locations of the external checkouts (ABIT resources, MATSim inputs). Then check:

miles config

docs.title: 3. Estimation environment
docs.text:
python -m venv ~/.venvs/biogeme
~/.venvs/biogeme/bin/pip install biogeme==3.3.5 pandas pyarrow matplotlib ipykernel nbformat
~/.venvs/biogeme/bin/python -m ipykernel install --user --name biogeme --display-name "Python (biogeme)"

Set python.biogeme in miles.toml to this interpreter.

docs.title: 4. The Java engines
docs.text:
SILOMILES-DayMATSim runner 
git clone https://github.com/msmobility/silo.git && cd silo
git checkout 3066ca9
git apply ../MILES/landuse/engine/silo_changes.patch
cp -R ../MILES/landuse/engine/src/* .
mvn compile -pl siloCore,extensions/schools,useCases/maryland

cd activity/engine/ABIT
mvn compile                     # main class abm.RunAbitMarylandLos

The engine reads its zone resources from the ABIT checkout set as paths.abit_home.

cd assignment/engine/matsim-run
mvn package                     # → target/baltimore-matsim-1.0.jar (MATSim 2024.0)

docs.title: 5. Data
docs.text:
MILES ships no data. Download the public sources and request the restricted ones as listed in Input data, into the workspace. After the land-use coefficients are written, copy the engine input files into the workspace with:

miles sync

docs.title: Repository layout
docs.text:
Code, coefficients and parameters live in the repository. Data and run outputs live in a workspace folder that you set in miles.toml.

MILES/
├── miles_cli.py            the `miles` command
├── miles_env.py            configured locations (repository, workspace, external checkouts)
├── miles.example.toml      configuration template → copy to miles.toml
├── population/              Synthetic population
│   ├── cvae/                generator: vaelib/ library, steps/00–09, run_all.py
│   ├── base_year/           fit_controls, zone_weights, jobs_2016, vacancies, external_workplaces, export_base_year
│   └── validation/          validate_population, validate_by_puma, figures
├── landuse/                 Land use (SILO) and school location
│   ├── engine/              SILO engine changes: silo_changes.patch, src/ (new classes)
│   ├── engine_inputs/       coefficient files and small tables read by the engine
│   ├── inputs/              builders of the engine inputs; assign_base_workplaces

docs.title: Where to look for…
docs.text: I want to… Go to Change a land-use coefficient landuse/engine_inputs/, written by landuse/coefficients/write_*.py Change an activity-model coefficient activity/parameters/ Change the network or a toll assignment/network/ Re-estimate a model miles estimate <model> or estimation/package/<stage>/<model>/ Run the full chain miles chain … (pipeline/run_chain.py)

docs.title: Run the chain
docs.text:
Every step is one miles command. Add --dry-run to any command to see what it would run.

flowchart LR
  s1[1 Population] --> s2[2 Coefficients] --> s3[3 Calibrate] --> s4[4 Land use] --> s5[5 Schools] --> s6[6 Activities] --> s7[7 Traffic]

docs.title: 1. Synthetic population (2016)
docs.text:
miles population all            # preprocess, targets, train, generate, workplaces, export, validate
miles population base-year      # fit to ACS controls, place in zones, external workplaces, export for SILO
miles population validate

Train or generate on their own: miles population train --tag full, miles population generate --tag full.

Output: hh_2016.csv, pp_2016.csv, dd_2016.csv, jj_2016.csv.

docs.title: 2. Estimated coefficients into the engines
docs.text:
miles landuse coefficients      # residential location, car ownership, workplace, schools, zone attributes; then sync
miles landuse base-workplaces   # 2016 workplaces with the estimated workplace model
miles landuse check             # engine utilities against the Biogeme estimates
miles activity parameters       # the MILES-Day parameter set (activity/parameters)
miles activity distributions    # survey distributions of frequency, start time and duration

docs.title: 3. Calibrate the land-use model (2016–2020)
docs.text:
miles landuse calibrate --rounds 4

The calibrated levers are written to landuse/calibration/calibrated_parameters.json.

docs.title: 4. Land use 2016–2024
docs.text:
miles landuse seeds --seeds 5 --parallel 2      # five seeds, out of sample, validated year by year
miles landuse run --seed 1 --end 2024           # one run

docs.title: 5. School location
docs.text: miles landuse schools --seeds 5                 # every year of every seed

docs.title: 6. Activities (MILES-Day, 2024)
docs.text:
miles activity replications --seeds 1-10        # ten replications on 10 % of households; picks the one closest to the mean
miles activity run --seed 1 --sample 0.1        # one run

docs.title: 7. Traffic assignment (MATSim, 2024)
docs.text:
miles assignment plans --activities activities.csv --legs legs.csv --pp pp_2024.csv --hh hh_2024.csv --out population_2024.xml.gz
miles assignment seeds                          # seeds 1–5, 100 iterations, 10 % sample
miles assignment run --seed 1 --toll assignment/network/roadpricing_HARB_2024.xml --plans population_2024.xml.gz
miles assignment validate

docs.title: The pipeline
docs.text:
miles chain runs the orchestrator with resumable bookkeeping (a marker per stage, a registry of completed stages and one log per stage):

Stage Command Land-use step miles chain silo-step Y0 Y1 [--skims TAG] Activities miles chain abit Y [--skims TAG] MATSim plans miles chain matsim-pop Y [--residents-only] [--no-gateways] Assignment miles chain matsim Y NETWORK SEED [--toll FILE] [--plans FILE] Skims from MATSim miles chain skims Y [--seeds a,b] Full loop with feedback miles chain loop [--max-inner 3] Smoke test (1 % sample) miles chain test Status miles chain status

Global options: --sample --iterations --threads --xmx --silo-xmx --seed --dry-run --force.

Feedback loop

miles chain loop feeds MATSim travel times back to land use and activities in two-year steps. The results in Calibration and validation use fixed skims.

docs.title: Re-estimate a model
docs.text:
miles estimate list
miles estimate car_ownership --check    # log-likelihood at the published estimates
miles estimate car_ownership            # full Biogeme estimation and comparison

docs.title: Data
docs.text:
MILES is built from public data, with two exceptions marked † (released by the agency on request). The tables list the data by the stage that uses them; bracketed numbers refer to the sources at the end of the page. The role of a dataset is estimation (a model is estimated on it), input (used as given), target (a calibrated parameter is matched to it) or test (used only for validation).

Files are placed in the workspace under data/raw/<source>/. The instruction sheet of each model in the estimation package lists the exact files and variables.

docs.title: Road network
docs.text:
Built by assignment/network/build_networks.py from OpenStreetMap (via pt2matsim) as network_2024.xml.gz, with the Key Bridge closed.

  • Free speed: posted speed, × 0.9 below 51 km/h; missing tags filled from MDOT SHA speed signs or the road-class median nearby (recode_speed_capacity.py, rules in SPEED_CAPACITY.md).
  • Capacity: per lane by road class (1,500 veh/h primary, 800 secondary, 600 tertiary and residential), Highway Capacity Manual bottleneck capacity on motorways and trunk roads.
  • Tolls: roadpricing_HARB_2024.xml, $3.00 per crossing of the Fort McHenry and Baltimore Harbor tunnels.
  • Count stations are matched to links by match_count_stations.py.

docs.title: Transit
docs.text:
assignment/transit/build_transit.sh builds the schedule from the GTFS feeds of the region's operators (MTA local and commuter bus, Light Rail, Metro, MARC, Charm City Circulator, county services, WMATA and others):

  1. merge the feeds (merge_gtfs.py);
  2. convert them for a weekday (Gtfs2TransitSchedule);
  3. map routes on the road network guided by the GTFS shapes (MapWithShapes);
  4. clean routes and set vehicle types;
  5. check plausibility.

Outputs: transitSchedule_2024.xml.gz, transitVehicles_2024.xml.gz, network_2024_pt.xml.gz.

docs.title: Input data in detail
docs.text:
These pages document the data that MILES reads: for each dataset a short description, the codebook of the variables the models use, descriptive statistics computed from the files, and the processing applied in the code. Bracketed numbers refer to the sources on the Data page.

Two datasets are released by the agencies on request and are not redistributed: the 2017/18 Regional Travel Survey and the zones and skims of the Maryland Statewide Transportation Model. For these, the pages give aggregate statistics only (weighted shares, means and counts); no record-level or zone-level values are shown, and cells based on fewer than 10 unweighted records are suppressed (shown as —).

Statistics are unweighted counts of records unless a table says weighted; weighted shares use the survey weights named in the codebook. Percentages are rounded to one decimal and may not sum to 100.

docs.title: American Community Survey microdata
docs.text:
The American Community Survey Public Use Microdata Sample (PUMS) [1] is the main source of household and person attributes in MILES. The Census Bureau releases it as one household and one person file per state and vintage; the files are public and are read directly from the downloaded zip archives. MILES uses several vintages, each for a different purpose. All shares below are weighted with the PUMS household (WGTP) or person (PWGTP) weights unless stated otherwise; dollar values are in 2016 dollars. Variable names are those of the PUMS data dictionaries of the Census Bureau.

docs.title: 2012–16 5-year file: population synthesis
docs.text: The generator of the synthetic population (a conditional variational autoencoder) is trained on the households and persons of the 2012–16 5-year PUMS [1] of the six states that the zone system touches: Delaware, the District of Columbia, Maryland, Pennsylvania, Virginia and West Virginia. Only the Public Use Microdata Areas (PUMAs) that contain a model zone are kept (96 PUMAs). The files are the standard state household (csv_h<st>.zip) and person (csv_p<st>.zip) files of the Census Bureau.

After the coverage scaling, the sample represents 4,704,934 households and 12,491,069 persons in households (253,029 household and 626,201 person records; mean weighted household size 2.52). The households are split by PUMA into a training (202,427), a validation (25,304) and a held-out test set (25,298 households); the test set is used only for the validation of the generator.

Missing values among the kept records (share of records): VEH 0.0 %; HINCP 0.0 %; GRNTP 73.9 %; SMOCP 27.6 %; TEN 0.0 %; ESR 19.2 %; SCHG 76.2 %; PINCP 17.9 %; JWTR 49.6 %; POWPUMA 49.6 %. Vacant units and group quarters are not kept, so vehicles, income and tenure are complete; GRNTP is reported for renters and SMOCP for owners only. ESR is missing for persons under 16, PINCP for persons under 15, SCHG for persons not attending school, and JWTR and POWPUMA for persons who did not work in the reference week.

docs.title: Processing
docs.text:
• Housing units only (TYPE = 1, NP ≥ 1); group quarters are not part of the synthetic population.
  • PUMAs without a model zone are dropped. In the five PUMAs that lie partly outside the zone system (West Virginia and Virginia), household and person weights are multiplied by the covered share of the PUMA.
  • Incomes are converted to 2016 dollars with ADJINC and binned (22 household, 16 person bins); income is not top-coded beyond the Census Bureau's own top-coding. Dollar values are redrawn within the bin at generation.
  • Occupation: age under 6 → child; ESR 1, 2, 4, 5 → employed; attending school (SCHG > 0) → student; ESR 3 → unemployed; age 62 or older and not in the labour force → retired; otherwise other.
  • The PUMS has no driver's licence variable. Persons aged 16 or older are coded as licensed unless their usual means of travel to work is bicycle, walking or other; persons under 16 are unlicensed.
  • Missing values are set to 0 before the recodes (no rent or owner cost, no income, not employed, not attending school); missing BLD and YBL become single-family detached and 1985.
  • Weights are clipped to 0–200 (households) and 0–500 (persons).

docs.title: 2014–18 5-year file: controls, car ownership and population test
docs.text: The 2014–18 5-year file [1] is centred on the base year 2016. It is used three times: (a) its person and household weights per PUMA are the controls to which the generated population is fitted (persons in households by age band 0–17, 18–34, 35–64, 65+; households by size 1 to 5 or more); (b) the Maryland households form the estimation sample of the car-ownership model; (c) the Maryland PUMA distributions (age, sex, employment, household size, income, vehicles, tenure, dwelling type) are the test of the base-year population.

docs.title: Mover households, 2014–18 and 2019–21: residential location
docs.text: The residential location models (region, zone and dwelling) are estimated on households that moved in the year before the interview, from the 5-year PUMS [1] of the six states. The 2014–18 file gives the estimation sample and a held-out validation sample; the survey years 2019–21 of the 2017–21 file (no overlap with 2014–18, same 2010 geography) give an out-of-time test. The dwellings occupied by all households that moved in within 12 months form the market from which the alternatives of the dwelling model are sampled.

docs.text: The 1-year person files [1] of the six states give the employment rates by single year of age and sex for every simulated year (the yearly targets of the employment model, pooled over the PUMAs of the model area and by state). The 2024 1-year household and person files of Maryland are the 2024 benchmark of the commute (work from home, departure time, travel time, mode and county-to-county flows), and the 2024 person files of the six states give the telework rates. The 2020 file is the Census Bureau's experimental release with experimental weights. PUMAs follow the 2010 definition up to 2021 and the 2020 definition from 2022.

docs.title: Validation benchmarks
docs.text:
The data on this page are used only to test MILES; no model is estimated on them. They describe travel and commuting in the forecast year 2024 (the time-use survey, the 2024 American Community Survey) or give an independent check of the base period (the National Household Travel Survey). The ACS microdata used for estimation and calibration are described on ACS PUMS. Bracketed numbers refer to the sources of the data page.

Shares and means are weighted with the survey weights. Cells based on fewer than 10 unweighted records are shown as "—". The study area or Baltimore region is Baltimore City and the counties of Anne Arundel, Baltimore, Carroll, Harford and Howard.

docs.title: American Time Use Survey
docs.text: The American Time Use Survey (ATUS) 17 records one diary day (4:00 to 4:00) of one person aged 15 or over per household, sampled from households leaving the Current Population Survey. MILES uses the multi-year files 2003–2024 (respondent, activity, summary and CPS files), public, downloaded from the Bureau of Labor Statistics. The files hold 252,808 diaries of 2003–2024. They test the number and type of activities per person and the commute in 2024 (activity/lib/reporting_2024/bench_atus.py).

docs.title: Processing
docs.text:
• Diary days on Monday to Friday that are not holidays, respondents aged 15 or over living in Maryland (pool Maryland) or in DC, Maryland or Virginia (larger pool, used where the Maryland sample is small).
  • The diary is cut into stays at every travel episode (activity code 18xxxx). A stay after a travel episode is an activity at the trip's destination; the first stay of the day is not an activity. A stay is at home when its episodes are at home or in the yard (TEWHERE 1); episodes without a place take the place of the previous episode.
  • The type of a stay away from home is the category with the most minutes: work (05), education (06), shopping (07) or other.
  • The commute is the last trip leaving home before the first work stay. Its travel time is the sum of the travel episodes up to the arrival at work, without stops; its mode is that of the trip arriving at work.

docs.title: National Household Travel Survey
docs.text:
The National Household Travel Survey (NHTS) 18 is the national one-day travel diary of the Federal Highway Administration. Two public files are used:

  • NHTS 2017 (household, person and trip files): an independent check of the base period of the regional survey, for residents of the Baltimore–Columbia–Towson metropolitan area (activity/lib/reporting_2024/obs_surveys.py). The national file holds 129,696 households, 264,234 persons and 923,572 trips.
  • NHTS 2022 (trip file): the trip length of car drivers and the share of business driving, used to check the traffic assignment (assignment/validation/regional_validation.py, coverage_estimate.py). The public 2022 file does not identify the metropolitan area; the closest class is the South Atlantic division, metropolitan areas of 1–3 million with heavy rail. The national file holds 31,074 trips.

docs.title: Employment
docs.text: Jobs enter MILES at three points: the 2016 job inventory of the synthetic population, the yearly job control totals of the land-use model, and the vacant share of jobs. Workplace counts come from the LEHD Origin–Destination Employment Statistics (LODES), county growth from the Quarterly Census of Employment and Wages (QCEW), and vacancies from the Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey (JOLTS). All three are public. Counties marked * form the study area.

docs.title: LODES workplace area characteristics
docs.text: Jobs by census block of workplace, all jobs (segment S000, job type JT00), LODES version 8 on 2020 blocks [3]. Maryland files 2016–2023 give the 2016 job inventory (by zone and job type) and the growth path of the job control totals; the files of the District of Columbia, Delaware, Pennsylvania, Virginia and West Virginia for 2017 give the zone employment used in activity-model estimation, and those for 2022 the 2024 benchmarks. The block crosswalk (md_xwalk.csv.gz) supplies the county and the block centroid. Downloaded from the LEHD server; no registration.

docs.title: Quarterly Census of Employment and Wages
docs.text: Employment and wages covered by unemployment insurance, by county, ownership and industry, annual averages, from the BLS open-data files [6]. MILES uses the county total for all ownerships and industries: its growth sets the county job control totals from 2016 to 2024 (later years keep the 2024 level), and the Maryland average annual pay deflated by the CPI gives the assumed real wage growth of 0.5 % a year. 594 county files are present (66 counties, 2016–2024).

• Counties merged in the zone system are summed: 51919 = Fairfax County, Fairfax City and Falls Church; 51942 = Prince William, Manassas and Manassas Park; 51951 = Frederick County (Virginia) and Winchester.
  • County jobs of year Y = 2016 base jobs × Q(Y) / Q(2016) × (1 − v(2016)) / (1 − v(Y)), with Q the QCEW employment and v the JOLTS job-openings rate of the county's state; within a county the zone and type split follows LODES.

docs.title: Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey
docs.text: Monthly state estimates of job openings, hires and quits, seasonally adjusted, total nonfarm, from the BLS public API [4]. The job-openings rate (openings as a percent of employment plus openings) sets the vacant share of jobs: 4.01 % in the 2016 base (Maryland) and the state rate of each later year in the job control totals. The Maryland quits rate of 2017–2019 sets the yearly rate of job-to-job changes.

docs.title: Land-use controls and county attributes
docs.text: These county-level data hold the land-use model to observed totals (population, new dwellings, housing units), describe counties in the residential location model (school quality, crime), convert dollars between years, and serve as validation targets (commuting and migration flows). All are public. Counties marked * form the study area.

docs.title: Population estimates and components of change
docs.text: Annual county population estimates of the Census Bureau, July 1 of each year [5]: the 2010–2020 intercensal estimates (by age and sex) for 2016–2019 and vintage 2025 (co-est2025-alldata.csv) for 2020–2025, so that the whole series rests on the 2020 Census. The population control of each land-use region in year Y is its synthetic 2016 population times the region's growth from 2016 to Y; 2026 extrapolates the 2024–2025 growth. Births and deaths of the components of change are validation targets for the demographic models (vintage 2020 up to 2020, vintage 2025 after).

docs.title: Codebook
docs.text: Variable Description Type Values / categories / units Used in SUMLEV Summary level integer 40 = state, 50 = county Land use STATE, COUNTY FIPS codes string joined to a 5-digit county code Land use YEAR Estimate date (intercensal file) integer 2–11 = July 1, 2010–2019 (year − 2008) Land use: control totals POPESTIMATE, POPESTIMATE<y> Resident population, July 1 integer persons Land use: control totals; validation BIRTHS<y>, DEATHS<y> Births and deaths, July to June integer events Land-use validation INTERNATIONALMIG<y>, DOMESTICMIG<y>, NETMIG<y> Net migration integer persons Description only

docs.title: Processing
docs.text:
• Counties are summed to the 44 land-use regions; a county split across regions is shared in proportion to its zones. Virginia composite codes of the zone system are expanded to their Census counties (51919, 51942, 51951).
  • Control of region r in year Y = synthetic persons of r in 2016 × PEP(r, Y) / PEP(r, 2016).
  • Validation: births per woman aged 15–50 and deaths per person, Maryland, from the components of change.

docs.title: Redistricting data: housing units by block
docs.text: Table H1 (occupancy status) of the 2010 and 2020 Census redistricting files (PL 94-171) for Maryland blocks [2]. Occupied units place synthetic households in zones within their PUMA; vacant units give the vacant dwelling stock of the 2016 base. Block locations: TIGER/Line 2010 block internal points (2010) and the LODES crosswalk (2020). The 2020 files of the District of Columbia, Virginia and West Virginia are also held but are not used in the base year.

docs.title: Codebook
docs.text: Variable Description Type Values / categories / units Used in SUMLEV, LOGRECNO Summary level and record number (2010 geographic header, fixed width) string 750 = block Population STATE, COUNTY, TRACT, BLOCK Block identifier (2010 geographic header) string 15-digit GEOID10 Population H1_total (H0010001) Housing units integer units Population H1_occupied (H0010002) Occupied housing units integer units Population: household placement H1_vacant (H0010003) Vacant housing units (2020: total − occupied) integer units Population: vacant dwellings GEOCODE Block identifier, 2020 string, 15 digits joins the LODES crosswalk Population INTPTLAT10, INTPTLON10 Block internal point, 2010 TIGER/Line float decimal degrees Population

docs.title: Processing
docs.text:
• 2010 blocks are read from the fixed-width geographic header (summary level 750) and segment 2 of the file.
  • Blocks are located by their internal point and joined to the zone polygons; points outside every polygon take the nearest zone.
  • Units of 2016 = units 2010 + 0.6 × (units 2020 − units 2010), by zone; the same rule gives vacant units.

docs.title: Building Permits Survey
docs.text: New privately owned housing units authorised by building permits, by county and year, annual county files (co<year>a.txt) [7]. Maryland counties build each year's permitted units in the land-use model: one-unit permits go to single-family detached, attached and mobile homes by the model's demand, 2–4 units to small multifamily and 5+ units to large multifamily. Permits also bound the land each county needs for new dwellings. The nine files hold 27,308 county rows (all states); Maryland has 24 counties in every year.

docs.text:
• Two header rows are skipped; Maryland rows are selected by state code 24.
  • Units are summed to three structure classes (1, 2–4, 5+). For the land each county needs, 2025–2026 are extrapolated at the 2016–2024 rate.

docs.text: Workers aged 16 and over by county of residence and county of work, ACS 2016–2020 five-year estimates, Table 1 [8]. docs.title: Road network

docs.title: Schools
docs.text:
The school location models of the land-use stage assign every student of the synthetic population to a school. They need an inventory of schools with a location and a capacity. MILES builds it from three federal collections of the National Center for Education Statistics (NCES): the Common Core of Data (public schools) and the Private School Universe Survey (private schools) [12], and the Integrated Postsecondary Education Data System (colleges and universities) [13]. The School Attendance Boundary Survey [14] gives the attendance zones of public schools. All four are public and are downloaded from the NCES web site into data/raw/nces/, data/raw/ipeds/ and data/raw/sabs/.

The inventory covers the six states with model zones: Maryland, the District of Columbia, Delaware, Pennsylvania, Virginia and West Virginia. Enrolment is taken as the capacity of a school. The inventory built from the most recent releases is used for the base year 2016 and for all later years.

docs.text: School directory and school membership files of the 2024–25 school year [12], with the EDGE geocodes of public schools for coordinates and county. The membership file is in long format (one row per school, grade and student group); MILES reads the school totals and the counts by grade.

docs.title: Processing
docs.text:
• Public schools: schools closed, inactive or not yet open are dropped, and so are schools without coordinates or students. Students by grade are summed to the bands K–5, 6–8 and 9–12; ungraded students follow the graded split of the school, or the CCD level where no graded counts exist. Prekindergarten is kept apart, as the synthetic students start at age 5.
  • Private schools: the K–12 total NUMSTUDS is split over the bands by the graded counts. Missing coordinates are taken from the EDGE private-school geocodes.
  • Post-secondary: active institutions; capacity is fall 2023 enrolment, or 0.8 × the 12-month headcount where fall enrolment is missing.
  • A record is kept for each band with at least one student. Points are placed in the model zones (point in polygon, EPSG:26918); Maryland schools outside every polygon go to the nearest zone; schools of other states outside the zone system are dropped.
  • The school day by band (start, duration) is the median of school trips of the 2017/18 Regional Travel Survey: elementary 08:35 and 7.0 h, middle 08:00 and 7.1 h, high 07:45 and 7.2 h, post-secondary 09:15 and 4.5 h.
  • Attendance boundaries: census-block housing units are placed in the boundaries covering the band's test grade and in the zones; the share of a zone's housing units inside a school's boundary enters the K–8 and high-school location models.
  • Code: landuse/schools/build_inventory.py, attendance_boundaries.py, school_data.py.

docs.text:
• Each direction of a station is matched to the nearest car link of a compatible class within 60 m (functional system 1–2) or 40 m (others), with the road identity checked against the MDOT route and the OSM name; ramp stations match ramp links only. docs.title: Regional Travel Survey 2017/18
docs.text: The 2017/18 Regional Travel Survey (RTS) is the household travel survey of the Baltimore and Washington regions. MILES uses it to estimate the activity models (tour formation, scheduling, destination, stop and mode choice), the workplace and school location models, and to validate the activity model on households not used in estimation. This page gives the codebook of the variables MILES reads and aggregate statistics of the survey.

The survey files are not redistributed with MILES.

The tables show aggregate statistics only. Shares are weighted with the weight of the unit of observation; a share or statistic resting on fewer than 10 unweighted records is shown as "—".

docs.title: Survey zone systems
docs.text: The survey codes locations by 2010 census tract and by the zones of the two regional models. The BMC TAZ 2010 layer has 2,922 zones (1,387 in the BMC region, the rest copies of TPB zones); the TPB TAZ 3722 layer has 3,669 zones. MILES places survey locations in its own zones through the census tract (internal point of the 2010 tract), because neither survey zone system has a crosswalk to the statewide model zones.

docs.title: Processing
docs.text:
• Trips: the cleaned trip file (deduplicated); purpose from o_activity and d_activity as above; mode from travel_mode: auto driver and motorcycle to car driver; auto passenger, school bus, paratransit, taxi and ride-hailing to car passenger; rail to rail; bus and private bus to bus; air, water and other dropped from mode shares.
  • Person types: worker (employment_status 0, a working student counts as a worker); student (student_status 1), by age band 5–10, 11–13, 14–17, 18+; retiree (employment_status 1); non-worker otherwise; persons under 5 have no tours.
  • Tours: closed home-based tours and work-based subtours of the tour file; open tours are dropped.
  • Split: households are split into an estimation half and a validation half, stratified by home county and household size (1 to 5 or more), with a fixed seed. Models are estimated on one half and validated on the other.
  • Survey population: home zone = the statewide model zone containing the internal point of the household's 2010 census tract; income = midpoint of hh_income_detailed; household members without a trip are added from hhsize, numworkers and numstudents, with age, gender and licence copied from a traveller of the same role.
  • Workplace and school: the zone of the work or school tract when it lies inside the zone system.
  • Parking: the survey records whether a driver paid for parking but not the amount; the car-driver utility uses the share of paid parking at the destination area.

docs.title: Zones, skims and census geography
docs.text: MILES uses the zone system of the Maryland Statewide Transportation Model (MSTM) for land use and activities, the zone-to-zone car skims of that model, transit skims computed on the 2024 schedule, and census tract geography to link survey and census records to zones. The zone system and the car skims are released by the Maryland Department of Transportation on request [21] and are not distributed with MILES; this page reports only aggregate statistics of them.

docs.title: Census tract geography
docs.text:
Four public Census Bureau and IPUMS files link census tracts, PUMAs and zones. They are used to place survey and PUMS records, which carry tracts or PUMAs, in the zone system.

  • TIGER/Line 2010 census tracts of the six states, and 2010 Maryland census blocks [28].
  • 2010 Gazetteer file of census tracts: internal point, land area and housing units [29].
  • 2010 census tract to 2010 PUMA relationship file [30].
  • IPUMS crosswalk of 2010 PUMAs to migration PUMAs and place-of-work PUMAs [31].
